title: decode-path sunburst latency-cost probe - lab notes
content:
TL;DR:
This is a working lab note that explores a compact visual + numeric comparison of decode-stage latency vs incremental cost across three serving configs (single-tenant A100, multi-tenant L40, and dedicated L4x-style small instance). The intent: capture how decode micro-path decisions (prefetch vs on-demand kv-cache, static tiling, smallbatch vs dynbatch) shift p50/p95/p99 while changing $/token. Not exhaustive — prototype for a sunburst-style breakdown that maps time budget -> dollar allocation.

Experiment summary:
- Model: open-llm-13b (fp16 baseline), int8 and q4_variants tested.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (dedicated), L40 (shared multiplex), L4x (small reserved).
- Traffic: synthetic chat sessions, 10k sessions, mixture: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-512), 10% long (>512).
- Key knobs: kv-cache prefetch window (0/32/128), decode tile size (16/32/64), batching mode (smallbatch, dynbatch).
- Measurement: client-observed p50/p95/p99, server decode CPU/GPU time, tokens emitted, infra $/hour (internal ratecard).

ASCII "sunburst" (conceptual):
Center = total decode time per request (ms). Radial rings = cost buckets that caused that time (kernel, kernel-queue, kv-prefetch, memory-COPY, scheduler wait). Width = relative $ contribution to that decode time across throughput-normalized baseline.

   [center] decode ms (p95)
      |
   /-- kernel (ms) ------
  |    \\              \
  |     \\  kv-prefetch 
  |      \\ (if enabled)
   \-- queue wait -------

Quick numerical snapshot (selected rows):
- Config A (A100, fp16, kv-prefetch=128, dynbatch):
  p50=38ms, p95=85ms, p99=210ms, tokens/s=620k, $/1M tokens = $4.1
- Config B (L40, int8, kv-prefetch=32, smallbatch):
  p50=52ms, p95=140ms, p99=420ms, tokens/s=280k, $/1M tokens = $9.8
- Config C (L4x, q4, kv-prefetch=0, dynbatch aggressive):
  p50=75ms, p95=210ms, p99=760ms, tokens/s=140k, $/1M tokens = $6.7

Observations (rough):
- Prefetch window shrinks p95 by ~18% on A100 when workload has >30% medium/long; prefetch cost is small relative to kernel time on A100 but dominates scheduling jitter on shared L40.
- Smallbatch reduces tail on shared hardware in light concurrency but increases $/token due to lower packing efficiency.
- Quantization (int8/q4) narrows $/token but increases p99 variance for long sessions (memory thrash + KV refill).
- p50 is an unreliable proxy for user experience when session mix contains a long-tail of >512-token interactions. p95/p99 are more correlated with perceived lag.

Cheap ascii cost-latency tradeoff table (normalized to Config A p95=1.0, cost=1.0):
- Config A: latency=1.0 cost=1.0
- Config B: latency=1.65 cost=2.39
- Config C: latency=2.47 cost=1.63

Interpretation:
- A100 remains best for latency SLOs (p95/p99) at modest cost; shared L40 shows big variability in p99 due to multi-tenancy queue spikes. L4x-style nodes are cost-competitive on $/token for sustained workloads but suffer severe tails for mixed session length.
- The sunburst view (next step) should visually link kernel-bound ms -> fraction of $/token by ring color. This helps product map which knob to expose to customers: e.g., prefetch window (latency-first) vs batch multiplier (cost-first).

Methodology notes / caveats:
- Internal ratecard used, not public pricing — numbers are directional.
- Synthetic traffic tries to replicate session mix from recent telemetry but lacks device-level network jitter.
- We did not run privacy-sensitive customer workloads here; this is lab-only.

Next steps:
1) Build lightweight D3 sunburst render in console experiments (prototype animation toggles: quantization, prefetch window, batch mode).
2) Run selected configs with real production traces (anonymized) for 24 hours and compute cost volatility percentiles.
3) Surface a compact UI card: "Expected p95 / $ per 1M tokens" with a slider for session mix and knob presets (latency, balanced, cost).

Open questions / unresolved:
- At what customer quota does L4x reserved become cheaper than A100 when factoring spike capacity and fallback policies? (need committed-utilization sim)
- Is there an automated rule-of-thumb for switching prefetch on/off based on observed session-length distribution? (policy vs learned classifier)

Notes to self: attach raw CSVs (kernel-ms, queue-ms, tokens) to JIRA-OBS-1227 and link the D3 prototype PR once ready.

-- end of lab note --
